lead: Turning a panic into a diagnostic breaks the tests that pinned the panic, and they do not look like your change.
body: A `#[should_panic(expected = "known gaps")]` guard fails with *"panic did not contain expected string"* while printing the new diagnostic, and a fixture helper's own `assert!(!diags.has_errors())` fails without naming the feature. Delete the guard — the `.nvst` case is its replacement — and split the fixture helper so the one test whose point is the diagnostic gets the `Diagnostics` back.
